title: Mock QCM / SQL joins & grain
summary: Synthetic QCM set for exercising AtlasNote question, attempt and review flows.
provenance: Original synthetic mock content created for AtlasNote UI testing. No private data, credentials or third-party content.

questions.prompt: An orders table has one row per order and order_lines has many rows per order. What is the safest first step before summing order-level revenue after a join?

options.text: Aggregate order_lines to one row per order before joining.
options.explanation: This aligns the detail table with order grain.

options.text: Join first and use DISTINCT on the final result.
options.explanation: DISTINCT can hide duplicates without preserving correct measures.

options.text: Switch the join to FULL OUTER JOIN.
options.explanation: Join type does not solve grain mismatch.

questions.explanation: Align grains before joining measures from different levels.
questions.followUp: Which checks would prove the result is still at order grain?

questions.prompt: Which window expression is best for selecting one latest row per customer when timestamps can tie?

options.text: RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY updated_at DESC)
options.explanation: RANK can return multiple rows on ties.

options.text: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY updated_at DESC, event_id DESC)
options.explanation: A deterministic tie-breaker gives one stable row.
COUNT does not identify the latest row.

questions.explanation: Use ROW_NUMBER with a deterministic ordering when exactly one row is required.
questions.followUp: When would RANK be more appropriate?

options.explanation: HAVING is evaluated after GROUP BY.
HAVING is not specific to NULLs.

questions.followUp: Why can moving a row filter from HAVING to WHERE improve performance?

questions.prompt: A LEFT JOIN followed by WHERE right.status = 'active' often behaves like what?

options.text: An INNER JOIN for that condition.
options.explanation: Rows with no right match have NULL status and are removed by WHERE.
No unmatched right-side rows are added.

questions.explanation: Filtering the right table in WHERE can remove unmatched left rows.
questions.followUp: Where would you place the right-side filter to preserve all left rows?
